text.p: French freight installations operator, Sogaris, said the extension to its existing facilities at Paris/Charles de Gaulle (CDG) airport was effectively fully-let.
The extension, which will enter service on May 1 1997 will provide an additional 10,000 sq. metres of warehousing and 2,200 sq. metres of office space.
The extension, costing 60 million francs, is being financed by a joint-venture company, 60 percent-owned by Sogaris and 40 percent by the Paris airports authority.

"While all the letting contracts have yet to be signed, we can say that all the space in the extension has been more or less snapped up and we are now in the position of having to turn down requests from potential occupants," Sogaris marketing and sales director, Jacques Salgues, told Reuters.

He declined to comment at this stage on the companies who would be occupying the extension but did say facilities covering between 400 sq. metres and 600 sq.metres, tailored to the requirements of small to medium-sized businesses, had been most in demand.
Cargo Service Centre (CSC) France, said it had let dedicated facilities covering 1,350 sq.m of warehousing and 310 sq.m of offices in the Sogaris extension.
CSC is a subsidary of Dutch airline, KLM and specialises in physical cargo handling, document handling and trucking.
Around 20 airfreight forwarders and agents occupy Sogaris existing Centre Logistique de Frret Aerien in CDG s freight zone.
This comprises 18,000 sq. metres of warehousing and 4,000 sq.metres of offices.
With airside access, the Sogaris centre is equipped with loading platforms for truck-borme freight and also houses a customs office.

"Given the buoyant level of demand for freight installations at CDG, it is very likely the Sogaris centre will see third -phase development although a firm decision has yet to be taken," Salgues added.
Sogaris is 80 percent-owned by public authorities in the Paris area with the remaining 20 percent owned by private investors.
